chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Abu Ishaq al-Nahawandi from Ahmad ibn 'Umar from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When you remember the favor of Allah upon you, and you are in a place where no one sees you, press your cheek to the ground. And when you are in a gathering of people, place your hand on the lower part of your belly, bow your back, and let it be humility for Allah, for that is more beloved, and it will appear that you are pressing (your hand) because you found something in the lower part of your belly.'
The Shaykh (Al-Shaykh al-Tusi) said: 'From the falling of the sun (the disk) until he says

key_terms.أَسْفَلِ بَطْنِكَ: The lower part of the belly
key_terms.غَمْزٌ: Pressing or nudging (used here to describe a subtle physical gesture)
key_terms.مَلَإٍ: A gathering or assembly of people

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended physical etiquette for showing humility during prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates the nuanced etiquette of humility (khushu') by prescribing extreme prostration in private to maximize sincerity, while adopting a modest, relatable posture in public to avoid ostentation (riya'). This guidance is embedded within Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* as part of the detailed jurisprudential exposition on prayer mechanics, specifically addressing the transition from obligatory to voluntary prayers without formal supplication (ta'qib).
